In one spacious luminous blue-gold Roman court at twilight, show exactly one complete seated Pythagorean philosopher-musician on exactly one complete plain stone bench. Across his lap he holds one complete large front-facing wooden lyre with EXACTLY SEVEN STRINGS. The seven strings are the only string-like lines in the entire image. Make them thick enough to count at native resolution, widely and evenly spaced across the open center of the lyre, each a continuous dark vertical from the plain top crossbar to its own fastening point on the soundbox. Count explicitly from left to right: string 1, string 2, string 3, string 4, string 5, string 6, string 7, then stop. No eighth string, no doubled line, no diagonal cord, no wire, no string ornament. Keep all tuning hardware small, plain, and visually subordinate; its count is not a subject. One hand plucks only central string 4, while the other holds the solid outer wooden arm without crossing or obscuring any string. Place the complete lyre and all seven strings against a quiet pale wall area, never over patterned clothing, so each line is unmistakable.
Across the upper-right sky show exactly seven—and only seven—complete separated mineral-colored wandering disks in a loose horizontal cadence: pale gray, muted ochre, restrained madder, brighter ochre, pearl white, dim umber, silver gray. Outside these seven disks the entire sky is empty of point lights: no stars, tiny white dots, flecks, sparks, sun, moon, lamps, fire, or extra disk. Render the sky only with continuous faded-lapis and ochre wash and fine horizontal cross-hatching, never light stipple. The seven disks and seven strings form a visual analogy without connecting lines, labels, diagrams, notes, or rays.
Scene/backdrop: broad limestone paving, one completely blank low wall, a distant quiet coastal horizon, and long coherent shadows. No tree, basin, column, arch, instrument case, book, tablet, scroll, extra furniture, extra person, or animal. Keep the set deliberately spare so count and historical uncertainty remain legible.
Style/medium: original Plinian natural-history folio painted directly across warm fibrous aged vellum; iron-gall contours, exceptionally fine visible cross-hatching and dry-brush abrasion; restrained translucent mineral washes of umber, lampblack, muted verdigris, faded lapis, quiet madder, and ochre; ancient, timeless, beautiful, rough in material yet polished in draftsmanship; cosmic-harmony dialect with sun-warmed limestone, tactile carved wood, seven crisp taut ink strings, and seven restrained sky disks; never photographic or glossy. No sky stipple.
Composition/framing: landscape 3:2, native 1536x1024; spacious low-oblique courtyard view. Place the complete figure, complete bench, and large front-facing lyre in the left-to-center-middle, occupying no more than half the canvas. Place the seven disks in the upper-right against otherwise empty sky. Reserve a broad band of unoccupied paving across the lower foreground and open sky beyond all disks. Keep the philosopher’s head, face, both arms, both hands and every finger, garment hems, legs and both sandaled feet, every bench corner and leg, both lyre arms, crossbar, seven strings, seven lower fastening points, soundbox, each of seven sky disks, wall, horizon, paving, and all primary shadows wholly inside generous breathing room. One continuous court only, never a music diagram, scientific chart, panel sequence, dark hillside panorama, split frame, or collage.
Historical and epistemic framing: present celestial harmony as a Pythagorean analogy reported by Pliny and preserve Pliny’s skepticism; do not imply that space literally produces these tones or that the depicted arrangement is current astronomy.
Constraints: exactly one complete adult, one complete bench, one complete front-facing lyre with precisely seven clearly countable strings, and exactly seven visible celestial disks with absolutely no other point lights; plausible ancient dress, instrument, architecture, and anatomy; opaque RGB/sRGB.
Avoid: wrong string count, extra string-like line, obscured string, five, six, eight, or more strings; any extra star, speck, or point light; extra people, animals, trees, basins, columns, books, tablets, scrolls, musical notation, sound waves, connecting lines, deity, trance, ritual, any subject touching an edge; lettering, captions, labels, numerals, pseudo-writing, signatures, logos, watermarks, visible page, sheet edge, decorative border, internal frame, grid, split panel, collage, repeated crop, magic glow, modern instrument, guitar, harp, photography, photorealism, glossy CGI, smooth digital rendering, or clipped primary subject.
Output intent: one unified full-bleed opaque landscape master, no transparency, no page edge, no internal framing, and no text-like marks anywhere.
